name: Budapest Gambit
summary: Against the queen-pawn opening, Black gives a pawn for fast piece play, then wins it back with active knights and a bishop check.

goal.title: Give a pawn for quick piece play, then win it back
goal.text: Black lets White keep an extra pawn at first. In return Black's pieces jump out fast: a knight attacks the extra pawn from the edge of the board, the other knight joins it, and a bishop comes out with check. Within a few moves Black wins the pawn back and enjoys the more active pieces.
plans: Attack the extra white pawn with a knight from the edge of the board, and bring the other knight to help.
Give a check with the dark-squared bishop to drag White's pieces onto awkward squares.
Put the queen next to the king to add pressure on the same pawn.
Take the pawn back as soon as it is safe, then castle.

variations.name: 4.Bf4: Rubinstein variation
variations.strategy: White protects the extra pawn with a bishop. Black brings out a knight, then checks with the bishop so White must block with an awkward knight that is now pinned. The queen joins on the open file. Once Black has more attackers than White has defenders, take the pawn back.

moves.note: White solidifies and prepares to develop the bishop.
Win the pawn back; Black is fully developed.

variations.name: 4.Nf3: Adler variation
variations.strategy: White protects the extra pawn with a knight, but Black's two knights soon win it back through a trade: take with the knight from the edge, swap the knights, and recapture. Material is level, Black's knight sits strongly in the center, and Black has no weaknesses. Be ready for White to grab the center with a pawn push.

moves.note: White defends e5 with a developing move.
Win the pawn back right away; the gambit has done its job.
Recapture; the centralised knight is strong.
White takes space in the center.

variations.name: 7.a3? Ngxe5!: the Budapest trap
variations.strategy: Here White makes a natural-looking mistake: attacking the pinned bishop. Black ignores it, takes the pawn with the knight and threatens a mating knight jump. It is the most famous trap in the Budapest; if White plays accurately the position is still fine for Black, but knowing the trap wins games.

variations.name: 3.e3: White declines the gambit
variations.strategy: If White does not take the pawn there is nothing to win back. Take the central pawn, build a central pawn of your own and develop calmly. The goal is the same: active pieces and a healthy center, and the position ends level.

variations.name: 3.Nc3: White develops instead of taking
variations.strategy: White ignores the gambit and develops. Take the center pawn, chase the queen with a developing move and pin the knight with the dark-squared bishop. Black's pieces come out with tempo and the position stays level.

variations.name: 3.d5: White closes the center
variations.strategy: The center is closed, so the fight moves to the wings. Develop, castle and prepare to break open the position later with a side pawn move, or aim for a strong knight outpost. Keep your pieces flexible and do not hurry.

variations.name: 2.Bf4: no gambit, take the center
variations.strategy: White develops the bishop and avoids the gambit, so Black simply takes the center. Take space with a pawn, hit the center from the side with another pawn, and develop the knights and bishops. Look for a trade of White's active bishop and a chance to open the center.

variations.name: 2.Nf3: no gambit, take the center
variations.strategy: White avoids the gambit with a quiet knight move, so Black simply takes the center. Claim space with a pawn, hit the center from the side, and develop with tempo. The queen can come out early to add pressure, and Black can gain space on the queenside.
